newsitem.title: UK: EIU upgrade makes Poland second best in E. Europe.
newsitem.headline: EIU upgrade makes Poland second best in E. Europe.

text.p: The Economist Intelligence Unit has upgraded Poland's credit rating by 10 points, boosting it to second place in its country risk league of east European nations, the EIU said on Monday.
The independent research group said in a statement the upgrade, from 40 to 30 points out of a maximum risk score of 100, partly reflected Poland's early repayment of its IMF debt.
The upgrade also followed the rise of foreign direct investment inflows since Warsaw completed its debt relief programmes with its official and commercial creditors in 1994.
"Poland is now rated second-best (after the Czech Republic) of the east European countries covered by the Economist Intelligence Unit's Country Risk Service," the EIU said.
Bulgaria, with 70 points, is at the bottom of the EIU's credit rating league, followed by Romania, Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic.
The EIU's senior economist for Europe, Merli Baroudi, said the current weakness in the German economy was making 1996 a more difficult year than 1995, when Poland clocked up 7.0-percent GDP growth.
But she said the EIU still expected the country's economy to expand by around 5.0 percent in 1996.

"With the country's debt-service ratio projected to fall below 10 percent in 1996, and official reserves likely to top the $20 billion mark, Poland is in a very good position to withstand a temporary slowdown in export growth," Baroudi added.
While the country has shown considerable improvement in its political and policy risk profile, the EIU said further upgrades would not come easily.

"The prospect of a further upgrade in Poland's creditworthiness will be difficult unless the coalition government curbs the inflation rate, undertakes politically sensitive reforms of the overly generous pension system and speeds up the privatisation process," Baroudi added.

Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and representatives of the banking sector met on Friday to discuss the sector's privatisation. More than 500 Polish firms are currently slated for praivatisation. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
